levels.title: Efficacy and clinical findings

factualObservations.observation: The report describes 810 randomized participants: 270 in the 12-week arm, 269 in the 6-week arm and 271 placebo. Continuous abstinence was 32.6% versus 7.0% at weeks 9–12 and 25.3% versus 4.4% at weeks 3–6.
Reported follow-up abstinence was 21.1% versus 4.8% through week 24 for the 12-week comparison, and 8.9% versus 2.6% for the 6-week comparison. Outcomes have different windows and placebo rates.

Safety analysis uses 809 exposed participants; placebo safety denominator is 270 rather than 271 randomized. The report lists serious adverse events but none judged treatment related, including one death in the 6-week group.
factualObservations.locator: paper Table 3 and footnote; Results adverse events

factualObservations.observation: The paper reports primary odds ratios of 6.3 (95% CI 3.7–11.6) for 12-week treatment and 8.0 (95% CI 3.9–16.3) for 6-week treatment. These are published estimates, not new calculations or an independent significance judgment.

levels.preliminaryInterpretation: Reported cessation outcomes support a bounded efficacy research discussion. Treatment-end and follow-up effects, denominators, uncertainty and harms must be reconciled before an owner benefit-risk assessment.

risksAndLimitations: No active comparator; 24-week follow-up does not establish long-term disease-outcome benefit or exclude uncommon harms.

levels.title: Statistical analysis

factualObservations.observation: SAP v1.0 cover is dated March 25, 2022; its embedded completion certificate reports March 29, 2022. Registry primary completion is December 23, 2021; public topline disclosure is April 27, 2022.
factualObservations.locator: SAP cover and PDF51–52; registry primaryCompletionDateStruct; dated sponsor article

factualObservations.observation: Protocol 16.1 already describes Hochberg with overall one-sided alpha 0.025. SAP 10.1 describes primary familywise-error control, conditional alpha propagation to secondaries and exploratory endpoints without multiplicity protection. Bonferroni appears in sizing assumptions.

SAP describes all-randomized efficacy analysis and exposed safety analysis, allowances for an interim missed visit, missing-as-failure rules and tipping-point sensitivity analyses. These rules require reconciliation with the reported implementation.
The paper names Hochberg control, but its reference 23 concerns false-discovery-rate methodology. The SAP specifies familywise-error handling; the citation discrepancy is unresolved.
factualObservations.locator: paper Statistical Analysis and reference23; SAP10.1.1

factualObservations.observation: The recorded primary rule uses one-sided 0.025 when both primary P values are <=0.025; otherwise the favorable comparison must be <=0.0125. Secondary alpha is conditional: 0.025 if both primaries pass, or 0.0125 for the corresponding secondary if only one passes. The third secondary requires both preceding secondaries to pass. No trial P values were transformed or re-tested here.
factualObservations.locator: SAP section10.1.1, PDF pages29–30; mathematical symbols visually checked against retained original
